title: Four-vectors and the Lorentz group
summary: The Minkowski inner product and the Lorentz group Λᵀ η Λ = η; its dimension and components; four-vectors by transformation law; four-velocity and four-acceleration with their invariants; raising and lowering indices.

objectives.description: Characterise the Lorentz group and its inverse, dimension and four components.
Use index lowering and the four-vector transformation law without conflating affine positions and displacements.
Compute four-velocity and four-acceleration and prove their invariant relations.
Show by a commutator why noncollinear boosts need ordered matrix composition.

preparation.description: Read Tong, Dynamics and Relativity, Section 7.3 The Geometry of Spacetime, especially 7.3.2 The Lorentz Group (reference-only; signature (+,−,−,−)).
Read Tong, Section 7.4 Relativistic Kinematics: 7.4.1 Proper Time and 7.4.7 Indices Up, Indices Down (reference-only).
Read Spacetime Physics Chapter 7, Section 7.2 Momenergy Arrow (pp. 191–195), for the book's four-vector picture.

activities.title: Lecture notes and primary reading
activities.instructions: Work through the notes with the assigned source open. Reproduce each worked calculation or derivation on paper, including its assumptions, before reading the next step. Write one question that remains unresolved.

activities.title: Problem sheet: calculation, explanation and transfer
activities.instructions: Attempt the problems independently first. Use one hint at a time if useful, and record which help you used. Show the reasoning that connects the model and its assumptions to each answer; compare the reference only after a substantial attempt.

activities.title: Return without the notes
activities.instructions: On a later study day, close the notes and reconstruct the core relation and its assumptions, then explain the failure case from the last problem. Compare with your saved work and correct one gap. This practice does not itself certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to judge the objectives: explain assumptions, complete the independent calculations and justify the final transfer/synthesis. The final exercise is the recorded checkpoint; its acceptance alone is not a claim that all course outcomes are mastered.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Any four numbers make a four-vector.
commonMisconceptions.correction: A four-vector is defined by its Lorentz transformation law.

commonMisconceptions.claim: The Lorentz group has only six transformations.
commonMisconceptions.correction: It has dimension six: six local continuous parameters, as well as distinct components.
The timelike tangent controls speed; acceleration is a different vector orthogonal to it.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A photon has a rest frame obtained by setting v=c.
commonMisconceptions.correction: That boost is not finite and photon proper time cannot parameterise a four-velocity.
